title: Manali to Leh
who: Classic route · the Himalayan highway by motorcycle
when: Mid-June to September, when the passes are open
vehicle: Royal Enfield or any adventure bike, 4–6 days
summary: About 430 km from the green Kullu valley to Ladakh's high desert, over five passes up to 5,300 m: Baralacha La, the 21 Gata Loops, the empty More Plains and Tanglang La. Tented camps at Sarchu and Pang, river crossings from snowmelt, and altitude to respect.

sources.label: Notes from Chetan: Manali to Leh by bicycle, July 2025
Vargis Khan: Pang to Manali by motorcycle

approximate: The usual overnight stops; the line follows the Manali–Leh highway.

stops.name: Manali
stops.text: The start, in apple orchards and deodar forest. Bikes checked, permits sorted.

stops.name: Atal Tunnel
stops.text: Under the Rohtang Pass by the 9 km Atal Tunnel into Lahaul, suddenly drier and starker.

stops.name: Keylong
stops.text: Lahaul's main town, a common first night.

stops.name: Baralacha La
stops.text: The first big pass, about 4,890 m, with broken road and snow walls early in the season.

stops.name: Sarchu
stops.text: A plain of tented camps on the Himachal–Ladakh border. Cold nights, no phone signal.

stops.name: Pang
stops.text: Up the 21 hairpins of the Gata Loops, over Nakee La and Lachulung La, to an army post and a few dhabas: one of the highest camps on the road.

stops.name: More Plains
stops.text: Forty kilometres of flat high plateau at 4,700 m, nomads' tents and wild asses.

stops.name: Tanglang La
stops.text: The last and highest pass of the highway, about 5,330 m.

photo.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Deeptrivia assumed (based on copyright claims).

stops.name: Upshi
stops.text: Down to the Indus valley and its monasteries.

stops.name: Leh
stops.text: Ladakh's capital under its old palace. Many ride on over the Khardung La to Nubra.
